subject: ProspectCorp RFI: SAST/DAST, pen test summary, SBOM and patch SLAs
messages:
From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@prospectcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@prospectcorp.com; security@prospectcorp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Security questionnaire — SAST/DAST, SBOM, pen test details

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement process we need details on your application security and vulnerability management posture. Attached is a short security questionnaire we run with every strategic vendor. Can you provide:

- High-level answers to the attached questionnaire (SAST/DAST tooling, cadence, vulnerability triage).
- Recent pen test summary (executive summary + any outstanding remediation items).
- SBOM availability and how often you refresh it for runtime/service dependencies.
- Patch / remediation SLAs by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low).

We'd appreciate responses by end of week (EOW). If you need a technical call, please propose times.

Attachments: ProspectCorp_Security_Questionnaire_20250710.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Alice Morris
Security Programs Manager
ProspectCorp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Security questionnaire — SAST/DAST, SBOM, pen test details

Alice —

Thanks for sending this over. Please find our formal response attached and an inline summary below to speed things up: Redwood_Security_Responses_ProspectCorp_20250711.pdf (pdf); redwood_sbom_snapshot_20250711.tar.gz (sbom snapshot).

SAST
- Primary tooling: Snyk (static analysis for OSS), internal linting + CodeQL for custom checks.
- Cadence: Continuous on PR; weekly scheduled scans across main branches.
- False-positive reduction: rule tuning + security engineer triage; auto-created Jira tickets for confirmed issues.

DAST / Runtime Scans
- Tools: OWASP ZAP for app-level DAST; authenticated scans against staging.
- Frequency: authenticated DAST cadence is bi-weekly, ad-hoc scans before major releases.
- Runtime detection: container image scans via Trivy in CI; RASP not currently deployed.

Penetration Testing
- Third-party pen tests annually (most recent: 2024-11-02). Executive summary attached: redwood_pen_test_summary_20241102.pdf (pdf).
- Outstanding items: all Critical/High findings from that test were remediated and validated within our SLAs; details redacted from public doc but available under NDA.

Patch & Remediation SLAs (typical)
- Critical: 72 hours after confirmed exploitability / vendor patch availability.
- High: 7 days.
- Medium: 30 days.
- Low: included in next scheduled maintenance cycle (quarterly).

SBOM
- We produce SBOMs for service artifacts (server binaries, container images) on every release; snapshot attached. Model weights and proprietary training datasets are excluded from SBOM for IP/legal reasons but third-party library dependencies used in model tooling are included.
- Format: SPDX + CycloneDX exports available on request.

Triage Flow
- Vulnerabilities ticketed in Jira (SEC-XXX). Severity assigned by product/security; SLA timers start on triage completion. We can share anonymized workflow screenshots if useful.

Next steps: happy to set a 30–45 minute technical call (Dev on this thread) to walk through specifics: SAST rule sets, authenticated DAST config, and SBOM scoping.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morris <alice.morris@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 10:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Security questionnaire — SAST/DAST, SBOM and SLAs (technical follow-up)

Hi Alice,

Following up with technical details Marissa mentioned; I'm the SE who owns infra security. A few clarifications based on common follow-ups:

1) SAST rule sets and scope
- We run CodeQL queries focused on injection, auth logic, secrets, and unsafe deserialization. Snyk provides OSS licensing + vulnerable dependency detection. We can export scan results for your review under an NDA.

2) DAST authentication and coverage
- Authenticated scans use service account creds and headless browser hooks; we test SSO flows for core user journeys. We can provide a replay script sample prior to a scan to validate coverage.

3) SBOM scope for model-serving
- SBOM includes base OS, language runtimes, pip/npm packages, and inference-serving binaries. Model artifact weights (e.g., weights.pt) are not enumerated; however, any third-party inference libraries (transformers, bitsandbytes) are listed.

4) Pen test details
- The 2024 third-party was performed by RedTeam Inc.; the executive summary is attached. Full report contains PII and contractual details, so we request an NDA and an on-site redaction review if you need full findings.

5) Patch windows and emergency fix process
- For a Critical production exploit we have a SE team on standby and a runbook to apply hotfixes; we aim for 72h because sometimes patching depends on vendor releases or kernel updates. For customers requiring shorter windows we can consider a paid accelerated remediation SLA (needs lead approval).

If helpful, propose a 30-minute call Tuesday 2025-07-15 at 10:00am PT; happy to demo our authenticated scan config and SBOM export.

Attachments: redwood_pen_test_summary_20241102.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@prospectcorp.com>

Subject: Re: RFI: Security questionnaire — SAST/DAST, SBOM and SLAs (request and SLA ask)

Marissa / Dev —

Thanks for the quick and thorough responses. A couple of asks before our security committee review:

- Can you provide a redacted full pen test report under NDA? Our legal team will execute an NDA if needed.
- We require the SBOM in CycloneDX JSON for automatic ingestion into our risk platform; the SPDX is fine but CycloneDX preferred.
- Regarding Critical patch SLA: our security team asks if you can commit to a 24-hour window for Critical findings during our pilot phase. Is there an escalation path and cost estimate for accelerating the SLA?

cc'ing Laura from your side per procurement's request so she can confirm any SLA exceptions.

If you can confirm NDA + CycloneDX SBOM + whether a 24-hour accelerated SLA can be accommodated (and any associated terms), we can move to procurement/contracting.

Best,
Alice Morris
Security Programs Manager
ProspectCorp
